title: Number of Children in Singapore Infected with Delta Variant of COVID-19 and Safeguarding Their Health Before Vaccination
what_it_is: Number of Children in Singapore Infected with Delta Variant of COVID-19 and Safeguarding Their Health Before Vaccination

sections.label: Child COVID-19 case age breakdown
sections.summary: Children under 12 are 0.6% of local infections, with cases split across four age groups.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Children below the age of 12 account for 0.6% of all local infection cases.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Amongst these COVID-19 paediatric cases in Singapore, 13.6% or 50 cases were aged zero to one, 22.6% or 83 cases were aged two to four, 20.7% or 76 cases were aged five to six and 43.1% or 158 cases were aged seven to 12.

sections.label: No severe child illness in Singapore
sections.summary: No child in Singapore has developed severe illness needing oxygen or ICU care, so severe illness rate is zero.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Fortunately, in Singapore, no child thus far has developed severe illness requiring oxygen supplementation or ICU care.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: So, the percentage of infected children that experience severe illness in Singapore is zero.

sections.label: Vaccine approval for children
sections.summary: The UK and US FDA may vaccinate children, and approval in Singapore depends on vaccine company applications.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: But we must learn the lessons of their experience, often hard-won, so that we can better protect our population here.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We read that the UK will be offering the COVID-19 vaccination to older children from 12 to 15 as soon as next week.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) may also authorise the use of the Pfizer vaccine for younger children from ages five to 11 by the end of the year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: When can we expect approval to be given in Singapore for our children to receive the vaccine and for what ages?

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Some of it will depend on the applications made by the vaccine companies.
